answer: Each hide is branded at the tannery and entered in the hide ledger with its weight and its curing date. A relic hide bought from a tanner in another county fails the ledger: at the nadir of the brand the mark must match the tannery's own iron, and a strange hide carries no brand at all. The forger pays 12,900 to run a tannery for a year, buy bark and lime, and still the falcon entry in the ledger is read at every market, so a hide whose brand was never entered is turned away.
